name: phase1_hamming_distance
description: Does the leakage track the static Hamming weight of the operand, or the
switching activity between consecutive operands? Everything measured so far
confounds them, and they are the two competing models in the literature.
Every working-set victim to date fills its buffer with one repeated 32-bit
word, so the Hamming distance between consecutive 32-byte transfers is zero
by construction and only the weight ever varies. Classical DPA attributes
the data-dependent draw to bits *flipping* on a bus -- charging and
discharging its capacitance -- and predicts nothing at all from a constant
value however heavy. The Hamming-weight sweep found +50.0 mW per set bit on
a constant stream, which under a pure switching model should not exist.
ws_l3_x8_ab splits the selector into two 32-bit words and alternates them
every 32 bytes, one ymm load wide, so consecutive transfers differ by
exactly HD(A, B) bits per word. Both words here have Hamming weight 16, so
the mean weight of the stream is 16 in every condition, identical to the
constant-word baseline. Weight is common-mode; distance is the only thing
that moves.
The alternation period decides which path sees the switching, and one
period cannot cover both. At 32 bytes every ymm load differs from the one
before it -- the toggling the load ports and the L1 read path see -- but a
64-byte line is then a fixed A-then-B composite, so consecutive line fills
from L2 or L3 are identical and that path sees no switching at all. So a
null on the 32-byte victim alone would be open to a fair objection: the bus
in question never saw a transition. ab64_hd32 repeats the largest contrast
on ws_l3_x8_ab64, which alternates every 64 bytes so consecutive lines
differ, at the cost of halving the load-to-load toggle rate.
Baseline in every hd run is A|A -- the same word in both halves, which
makes the fill bit-identical to plain ws_l3_x8 holding A.
A = 0x05A5E34F, HW 16, the sweep's hw16_a operand
run       B             HD    pure-HD prediction   pure-HW prediction
hd16_a    0xCDF62C0C    16         +0.80 W              0
The pure-HD column prices a flipped bit at the 50.0 mW the sweep measured
for a set bit, so the fitted slope is directly comparable: mW per flipped
bit against mW per set bit. hd32 is the maximum distance available at fixed
weight, B = ~A, where every bit flips on every transfer.
Three controls, because a mixture of two operands is not only a distance
change:
aa_hd0      A/A on the dual victim. Gate.
ab_equiv    0 -> A|A on the dual victim. With both halves equal this is
bit-identical to ws_l3_x8, so it must reproduce the sweep's
hw16_a (+1.133 W). Validates the new fill against the old.
anchor_hw16 the same contrast on ws_l3_x8 itself, in this session.
anchor and ab_equiv should agree; they are the same
measurement through two code paths.
placement   A -> ~A on ws_l3_x8, both homogeneous, both HW 16. The hd32
condition is half ~A by volume, so if ~A is intrinsically
cheaper or dearer than A this run measures the whole of that
difference and hd32 inherits about half of it. Elsewhere in
this data two HW-16 patterns differ by 0.071 W, which puts
the floor for a null at roughly +/-35 mW -- against a 1.6 W
prediction at hd32.
Read with:
analysis.aggregate <dir>
analysis.hwfit --axis hd --labels 'hd*' <dir>
A slope near 50 mW/bit means switching dominates and the weight effect was
an artifact of measuring a constant stream. A slope near zero, with hd32
inside the placement control, means this leakage is genuinely static -- a
Hamming-weight channel, not a Hamming-distance one -- which is the more
interesting outcome and the one the sweep's linearity already implies.
Driver settings match phase1_hamming_weight so anchor_hw16 is directly
comparable to it; the seeds differ.

runs.label: aa_hd0
runs.comment: A/A gate, both conditions A|A. Predict 0.

runs.label: hd16_b
runs.comment: A|A -> A|0x39B065F4. HD 16, different bits; pairs with hd16_a to separate distance from placement.

runs.label: hd32
runs.comment: A|A -> A|~A. HD 32, the maximum at fixed weight.

runs.label: ab64_hd32
runs.comment: A|A -> A|~A at 64-byte alternation: consecutive cache lines differ instead of consecutive loads. Same HD, different path.

runs.label: ab_equiv
runs.comment: 0 -> A|A on the dual victim. Must reproduce the sweep's hw16_a, +1.133 W.

runs.label: anchor_hw16
runs.comment: Session anchor, and the old code path for ab_equiv to be compared against.

runs.label: placement
runs.comment: A -> ~A, both homogeneous, both HW 16. Bounds how much of hd32 is composition rather than switching.
